q: Which structure–function statement applies to BOTH mitochondria and chloroplasts?
options: A small inner space (intermembrane space or lumen) lets a steep proton gradient form quickly
Large stacks of thylakoids provide a big surface area for absorbing as much light as possible
Rubisco dissolved in the matrix fixes CO2 into organic compounds using ATP from the cristae
Cristae contain chlorophyll and photosystems, allowing photophosphorylation to take place
explanation: Both organelles make ATP by chemiosmosis: protons are pumped into a narrow compartment – the mitochondrial intermembrane space or the thylakoid lumen – so a high H+ concentration develops from relatively few protons, maximising the force driving H+ through ATP synthase. Both also have a double membrane, 70S ribosomes and naked circular DNA.
